Sugar, either in the form of granulated sugar1-5 or pastes composed of caster sugar and icing sugar,6,7 has been used successfully in the treatment of wounds (p.1585) in- cluding mediastinitis after cardiac surgery,1,3 large abscesses and bed sores,6,7 diabetic ulcers,2,4 and recurrent bone infections after surgical debridement in patients with leprosy.5 Debridement of the wound is believed to be due partly to the osmotic effect of sugar and partly to the mechanical cleansing action but it is not known how sugar stimulates granulation tissue to form.6,7 Once granulation tissue is well established and the wound is shrinking, an alternative wound preparation, such as an alginate, hydrocol- loid, or hydrogel, should be used as sugar pastes cause bleeding.8 Sugar is also effective at deodorising malodorous wounds.
